paṭidātabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative singular agreeing with cīvaraṃ; passive potential participle ('fit to be given back') in the Vinaya rule on the saṅkamanīya robe.
paṭidātabbaṃ.example_1: Pañcame cīvarasaṅkamanīyanti saṅkametabbaṃ cīvaraṃ, aññissā santakaṃ anāpucchā gahitaṃ puna paṭidātabbaṃ pañcannaṃ aññataraṃ cīvaranti attho.
paṭidātabbaṃ.translation_1: In the fifth [case], 'the robe that should be given back' means a robe that ought to be moved; specifically, it refers to any one of the five robes belonging to another [bhikkhunī] that was taken without asking and must be returned.

atāvakālikatāti.meaning_2: state of not being temporary; permanence
atāvakālikatāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formed with -ti (tā) from atāvakālika, 'not temporary'. The word in the text carries the quotation clitic -ti: atāvakālikatā + ti; the -ti of the headword itself is the suffix, not the quotative, so the entry is for atāvakālikatā. Nominative singular, one of the three aṅgas in the sentence.
atāvakālikatāti.example_1: Samaṇacīvaratā, ṭhapetvā sahadhammike ca mātāpitaro ca aññesaṃ dānaṃ, atāvakālikatāti imānettha tīṇi aṅgāni.
atāvakālikatāti.translation_1: The three factors here are: its status as a contemplative robe, giving it to others setting aside co-religionists and parents, and [the giving] not being temporary.

pariyiṭṭhimatteyeva.meaning_2: mere searching; mere act of seeking
pariyiṭṭhimatteyeva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, formed as pariyiṭṭhimatte + eva with sandhi. Means 'only as far as searching'.
pariyiṭṭhimatteyeva.example_1: Itarathā hi pariyiṭṭhimatteyeva pārājiko bhaveyya, na cetaṃ yuttaṃ.
pariyiṭṭhimatteyeva.translation_1: Otherwise, one would be defeated merely by having sought it, and this is not suitable.

tuvaṭṭananti.meaning_2: lying down; sleeping; the act of lying down
tuvaṭṭananti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of the compound dvinnaṃ tuvaṭṭanan ti, accusative singular with the quotation particle -ti attached; the compound means 'lying down (of two [monks])'.
tuvaṭṭananti.example_1: Ekamañcatā, dvinnaṃ tuvaṭṭananti imānettha dve aṅgāni.
tuvaṭṭananti.translation_1: The state of being on a single bed and the two lying down are the two factors here.

ubbaḷhāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the sentence it is feminine instrumental singular agreeing with ubbaḷhāya, probably referring to being oppressed or expelled by someone. The form ubbaḷhāya is an unusual spelling for ubbāhitāya, the past participle of ubbāhati. The root connection is uncertain.
ubbaḷhāya.example_1: Idha sattāhakaraṇīyena vā kenaci ubbaḷhāya vā āpadāsu vā gacchantiyā ummattikādīnañca anāpatti.
ubbaḷhāya.translation_1: Here, there is no offense for one who is going due to a seven-day necessity, due to being forced out by someone, due to misfortunes, or for the insane and so on.

añchitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used in the clause yattakaṃ hatthena añchitaṃ hoti (whatever has been pulled by hand); nominative singular neuter agreeing with the subject of hoti.
añchitaṃ.example_1: Kanteyyāti ettha yattakaṃ hatthena añchitaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ takkamhi veṭhite ekā āpatti.
añchitaṃ.translation_1: Regarding ‘spin’, there is one offense when that amount which has been pulled by hand is wound onto a spindle.

ajjhoharaṇiyaṃ.meaning_2: to be eaten; to be consumed; ingestible
ajjhoharaṇiyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it qualifies an omitted noun (likely bhojana) and is in the nominative singular. The word is formed from ajjhoharaṇa (the act of eating) with the suffix -iya, meaning 'fit to be eaten'.
ajjhoharaṇiyaṃ.example_1: Aññatra udakadantaponā ajjhoharaṇiyaṃ, ṭhapetvā pañca sahadhammike aññassa sahatthā dānanti imānettha dve aṅgāni.
ajjhoharaṇiyaṃ.translation_1: Except for the toothpick, the ingestible food, setting aside the five co-religionists, and the act of giving to someone else with one's own hands—these are the two factors here.

anissajjanaṃ.meaning_2: not relinquishing; not giving up; failure to abandon
anissajjanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] One of four factors (aṅga) regarding robes; nominative singular in the text.
anissajjanaṃ.example_1: Āvasathacīvaratā, catutthadivasatā, dhovitvā anissajjanaṃ, anuññātakāraṇābhāvoti imānettha cattāri aṅgāni.
anissajjanaṃ.translation_1: The fact of it being a monastery robe, the fourth day, not relinquishing after washing, and the absence of an unauthorized cause—these are the four factors here.

hatthiassarathadhanutharusippaāthabbaṇak.meaning_2: consisting of such things as elephants, horses, chariots, bows, swords, crafts, the Āthabbaṇa and Khilana spells, subjugation, the Sosāpaṇa mantras, the use of poison, and so on
hatthiassarathadhanutharusippaāthabbaṇak.construction: hatthi + assa + ratha + dhanu + tharu + sippa + āthabbaṇa + khilana + vasīkaraṇa + sosāpana + manta + agada + payoga + ādi
hatthiassarathadhanutharusippaāthabbaṇak.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A long bahubbīhi compound describing the kinds of lowly craft (tiracchānavijjā); the text form is the accusative singular qualifying vijjaṃ. Possibly hatthi + assa + ratha + dhanu + tharu + sippa, with tharu likely meaning 'sword'; vasīkaraṇa and sosāpana are the names of spells.
hatthiassarathadhanutharusippaāthabbaṇak.example_1: Navame tiracchānavijjanti yaṃkiñci bāhirakaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ hatthiassarathadhanutharusippaāthabbaṇakhilanavasīkaraṇasosāpanamantāgadappayogādibhedaṃ parūpaghātakaraṃ vijjaṃ.
hatthiassarathadhanutharusippaāthabbaṇak.translation_1: In the ninth, 'lowly arts' means whatever secular, unbeneficial lore that causes harm to others, such as [arts related to] elephants, horses, chariots, bows, swords, [or] spells such as the Āthabbaṇa, Khilana, Vaśīkaraṇa, and Sosāpaṇa mantras, or the application of poisons.

aparipūriyā.meaning_2: because of the non-completion (of); from the non-fulfilment (of)
aparipūriyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Looks like an absolutive-like or instrumental/ablative feminine form of aparipūri, used with ubhinnaṃ: 'both not being complete'. Not a regular part of the word list; might belong to aparipūrati.
aparipūriyā.example_1: Ubhinnaṃ aparipūriyā ‘‘ bhikkhuniyo, ayyā, ayye pavārenti diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā, vadantāyyā bhikkhuniyo anukampaṃ upādāya, passantiyo paṭikarissantī ’’ ti ca,‘‘ bhikkhuniyo, ayya, ayyaṃ pavārenti diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā, vadatāyyo bhikkhuniyo anukampaṃ upādāya, passantiyo paṭikarissantī ’’ ti ca,‘‘ ahaṃ, ayyā, ayye pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā … pe … vadantu maṃ, ayyā, anukampaṃ upādāya, passantī paṭikarissāmī ’’ ti ca,‘‘ ahaṃ, ayya, ayyaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā … pe … vadatu maṃ, ayyo, anukampaṃ upādāya, passantī paṭikarissāmī ’’ ti ca evaṃ tikkhattuṃ vattabbaṃ.
aparipūriyā.translation_1: If both [communities] are not filled, 'The bhikkhunīs, venerable ones, invite [you], venerable ones, [to criticize them] regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. Let the venerable ones speak to the bhikkhunīs out of compassion. Seeing [it], they will remedy it,' and 'The bhikkhunīs, venerable sir, invite [you], venerable one, [to criticize them] regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. Let the venerable one speak to the bhikkhunīs out of compassion. Seeing [it], they will remedy it,' and 'I, venerable ones, invite [you], venerable ones, [to criticize me] regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. Let the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing [it], I will remedy it,' and 'I, venerable sir, invite [you], venerable one, [to criticize me] regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. Let the venerable one speak to me out of compassion. Seeing [it], I will remedy it,' should thus be said three times.

pasākhoti.meaning_2: lower part of the body (from the navel to the knees); fork; main branch
pasākhoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is pasākhoti = pasākho + iti, with the quotation particle -ti. The entry is for the main word pasākha.

upajjhāyininti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] From the sentence upajjhāyininti, i.e. upajjhāyini + iti; the quoted form here is feminine upajjhāyinī, but the base entry is the masculine upajjhāya. In the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī comment on upasampadā, it refers to the bhikkhunī's preceptor (pavattinī); the suffix -inī marks the feminine.
upajjhāyininti.example_1: Navame vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattininti vuṭṭhāpitaṃ pavattiniṃ yāya upasampāditā, taṃ upajjhāyininti attho.
upajjhāyininti.translation_1: In the ninth, 'preceptor who has given Acceptance' means the preceptor who has brought [the student] to maturity; the one by whom she was given higher ordination—that preceptor is the meaning.

nivārīyamānā.meaning_2: being prevented; being restrained; being refused
nivārīyamānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive present participle of nivāreti, feminine nominative singular agreeing with the subject (a bhikkhunī).
nivārīyamānā.example_1: Chaṭṭhe alaṃ tāva te ayye vuṭṭhāpitenāti vuccamānāti vuṭṭhāpanasammutiyā yācitāya saṅghena upaparikkhipitvā ‘‘ yasmā bālā abyattā ca alajjinī ca hoti, tasmā alaṃ tāva tuyhaṃ upasampāditenā ’’ ti evaṃ nivārīyamānā.
nivārīyamānā.translation_1: In the sixth, 'having been told: Enough, venerable, of your giving Acceptance for the time being' refers to one who is being restrained, saying: 'Since you are foolish, unwise, and shameless, it is enough for you to give Acceptance,' after the Community has inquired about the request for the agreement to ordain.

svāssā.meaning_2: that is her; that for her
svāssā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sā (she) + assā (genitive/dative of idaṃ, feminine). The PEU entry svāsa is unrelated.
svāssā.example_1: Atha vā gharaṃ viya gharasāmikā ayampi purisasamāgamaṃ alabhamānā sokaṃ āvisati, iti yaṃ āvisati, svāssā āvāso hotīti sokāvāsā.
svāssā.translation_1: Alternatively, just as a mistress of a house enters a house, so too she enters into sorrow when she cannot find an encounter with men; thus, whatever she enters into, that is her dwelling-place, so it is 'a cause of grief'.

pārivāsiye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, agreeing with the probation (pārivāsiye). Alternative spelling pārivāsiya.
pārivāsiye.example_1: Etasmiṃ pārivāsiye puna chandapārisuddhiṃ anāharitvā kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘ pārivāsikachandadānenā ’’ ti.
pārivāsiye.translation_1: In this probation, it is not proper to perform an act without again bringing forward the purity of consent; it is in reference to this that it was stated 'by giving of consent, postponed overnight'.

gambhinisikkhāpadasadisānevāti.meaning_2: just like the rule about [the] pregnant [woman] even; even identical with the pregnant-woman training rule and so on, it is said
gambhinisikkhāpadasadisānevāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi at the end of a sentence in a commentary. Resolves as gambhinī-sikkhāpada-sadisāni eva iti: gambhinī is 'pregnant woman', the Vinaya rule is named for her; sadisa (Pāḷi sadisāni, neut plural agreeing with samuṭṭhānādīni, here written sadisāne- with sandhi of -i + e-). The -ti is the quotation particle.
gambhinisikkhāpadasadisānevāti.translation_1: The origins and so on are the same as for [the rule on] the pregnant woman.

ummaddanaparimaddanāti.meaning_2: rubbing and massaging; kneading and rubbing all over
ummaddanaparimaddanāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of the compound ummaddanaparimaddanāti (ummaddanaparimaddana + iti), quoted as the name of a bhikkhunīsikkhāpada. It is also the object of ummaddanaparimaddanāhi; here it is nominative/accusative neuter singular.
ummaddanaparimaddanāti.example_1: Tatrāyaṃ saṅkhepato asādhāraṇasikkhāpadesu samuṭṭhānavinicchayo – giraggasamajjā cittāgārasikkhāpadaṃ saṅghāṇī itthālaṅkāro gandhavaṇṇako vāsitakapiññāko bhikkhuniādīhi ummaddanaparimaddanāti imāni dasa sikkhāpadāni acittakāni lokavajjāni akusalacittāni.
ummaddanaparimaddanāti.translation_1: Here is the summary of the determination of the origin for the unshared training rules: the Giraggasamajjā rule, the Cittāgāra training rule, the Saṅghāṇī [rule], Women's ornaments, Scented powders, Perfumed sesame powder, and the [training rule on] rubbing and massaging [bhikkhunīs]—these ten training rules are without thought, worldly faults, and unwholesome minds.

bhāṇavārapaamāṇāya.meaning_2: of the measure of a bhāṇavāra; amounting to (so many) recitations
bhāṇavārapaamāṇāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written bhāṇavārapaamāṇāya in the text, probably a typo for bhāṇavārapamāṇāya; feminine instrumental singular agreeing with pāḷiyā.
bhāṇavārapaamāṇāya.translation_1: Amounting to twenty-two bhāṇavāras of Pāli text.

karaṇasampattijanitasuviniggatamadhaurod.meaning_2: endowed with the charm of sweet, well-uttered, noble speech produced by skill in articulation
karaṇasampattijanitasuviniggatamadhaurod.construction: karaṇa + sampatti + janita + su + viniggata + madhu + urodāra + vacana + lāvaṇṇa + yutta
karaṇasampattijanitasuviniggatamadhaurod.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular describing the author; a long bahubbīhi compound. The text is from the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī prose introduction.
karaṇasampattijanitasuviniggatamadhaurod.example_1: Paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyappaṭimaṇḍitena sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayasamuditena sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhaṇasamatthena paññāveyyattiyasamannāgatena tipiṭakapariyattippabhede sāṭṭhakathe satthusāsane appaṭihatañāṇappabhāvena mahāveyyākaraṇena karaṇasampattijanitasuviniggatamadhaurodāravacanalāvaṇṇayuttena yuttamuttavādinā vādīvarena mahākavinā pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāre chaḷabhiññādippabhedaguṇappaṭimaṇḍite uttarimanussadhamme suppatiṭṭhitabuddhīnaṃ theravaṃsappadīpānaṃ therānaṃ mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ vaṃsālaṅkārabhūtena vipulavisuddhabuddhinā buddhaghosoti garūhi gahitanāmadheyyena therena katā ayaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇī nāma pātimokkhavaṇṇanā –
karaṇasampattijanitasuviniggatamadhaurod.translation_1: This explanation of the Pātimokkha called Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī was composed by the Elder known by the name Buddhaghosa, who is adorned with perfectly pure faith, wisdom, and energy; who is endowed with an abundance of virtues such as morality, good conduct, rectitude, and gentleness; who is capable of immersing himself deeply in the profundity of his own doctrine and other doctrines; who is endowed with sharpness of wisdom; who possesses unhindered power of knowledge in the Teacher’s dispensation, which has divisions of the Tipiṭaka and its commentaries; who is a great grammarian; who is joined with the beauty of sweet and noble speech produced by perfection in articulation; who is a speaker of appropriate and delightful words; who is a supreme debater; who is a great poet; who is surrounded by the analytical knowledges; who is adorned with virtues of the six higher knowledges and so on; whose wisdom is well-established in the superhuman Dhammas; and who is an ornament to the lineage of the Elders residing in the Great Monastery, who are like lamps of the lineage of Elders.
